description: HTMLTrust revocation-list keyid-alias immunity vector 02: demonstrates why a revoked entry MUST be matched by publicKeyHash rather than by keyid string. Reuses the revoked key material from revocation-01.json.
note_urlAliases: Each string above is a different keyid literal from canonicalKeyid, and the URL Standard would serialize every one of them (and canonicalKeyid) to the identical https://keys.example/alice-2024.json if keyid were merely used to construct a fetch. It is not merely used that way: Section 8.2 requires the retrieved key document's kid to equal the literal keyid text byte for byte, not a URL-Standard-normalized form of it. The key document at this location has kid "https://keys.example/alice-2024.json", so resolving any alias above fails that comparison and MUST return malformed-key-document at Section 12 Step 5, before a revocation list is ever consulted. publicKeyHash above is the hash produced only by resolving canonicalKeyid itself; a signature carrying an alias here never reaches the point of computing it.
note_forbiddenForms: Each string above differs from canonicalKeyid only by an added query or fragment component, which Section 5.1 forbids outright in a URL keyid. A verifier MUST reject each with key-resolution-failed at Step 1 of Section 12, before any resolution or revocation-list consultation, rather than relying on canonicalization to strip the difference away.
note_didWebCaseVariant: did:web resolution (Section 8.1) lowercases the host when constructing the DID document URL, so both strings fetch the identical DID document. That document's own top-level id can equal only one spelling, the canonical did:web:example.com, so resolving the alias did:web:EXAMPLE.com against it fails Section 8.1's required id equality with key-resolution-failed -- the same outcome the URL aliases above reach under Section 8.2, for the same reason: an identifier that differs from the document's own declared identity does not resolve, even when the underlying fetch lands on the right document.
